name: Penang Bridge International Marathon
short_description: The Penang Bridge International Marathon is a full marathon, half marathon, and 10 km race held on Penang Bridge, George Town, Malaysia on December 13, 2026.
ai_summary: The Penang Bridge International Marathon is a road race scheduled for December 13, 2026, held on Penang Bridge in George Town, Malaysia. It offers three distance options: a full marathon (42.195 km), a half marathon (21.1 km), and a 10 km run. The event is organized by the Penang State Tourism Development office with support from PETACE.

core_facts.organizer: Penang State Tourism Development office (supported by Penang State EXCO for Tourism and Creative Economy - PETACE)

pros: The Second Bridge is closed to traffic for the race
A seven-hour marathon limit, with a medal and finisher tee for every finisher inside it
21 aid stations on the marathon, nearly all with water, 100 Plus and toilets
Prize money ten deep: 3:46:16 was tenth in the 2025 women's open marathon
Low entry fees: RM150 for the marathon at the 2025 general rate
cons: A 1.30am start in Batu Kawan means a late-night shuttle from George Town
Humid night air: 25°C with a 23°C dew point at the 2025 start, and little breeze
An out-and-back on one bridge, run mostly in the dark
Only two age groups, Open and Veteran
Getting into the start pens was confusing in 2025

faqs.question: When is the Penang Bridge International Marathon held?
faqs.answer: The race is scheduled for December 13, 2026. It takes place on Penang Bridge in George Town, Malaysia, and includes full marathon, half marathon, and 10 km distance options for participants.

faqs.question: What distances can I run in this race?
faqs.answer: Participants can choose from three distances: a full marathon of 42.195 km, a half marathon of 21.1 km, or a 10 km run, all held on the Penang Bridge course in George Town, Malaysia.

faqs.question: Who organizes the Penang Bridge International Marathon?
faqs.answer: The event is organized by the Penang State Tourism Development office, with support from the Penang State EXCO for Tourism and Creative Economy (PETACE), reflecting official state involvement in Malaysia.
